scope: Corrections to the 46f3553d3 source/test bundle. Still source-only; no owner, workflow, frontend or production claim.

corrections.detail: The Quality-return receipt source is now scoped by Company, return and actor. It returns only matching receipts and re-reads the exact rows, so unrelated receipt history cannot exhaust the 10k/2 MiB budget or be mistaken for a local approval. The prior global CTE and global bound were removed.

The Records link oracle now checks the actual TypeScript bind order (companyId, id, id2), the caller's id2=id assignment, and the selected-request bind values. Caller duties for lock-before-snapshot, canonical search_path and non-BYPASSRLS role are documented on both source witnesses.
The inline Bun oracle is now named and documented as the inner target-scope branch only. It stubs assignment, target and purchase hooks and is not installed-policy authorization parity.
Removed the stale MigrationPhase import and formatted the roster source/test. cargo clippy --locked -p erpx-server-runtime --all-targets -- -D warnings passes.

knownLimits: The Records witnesses require the caller to acquire the source lock before the first protected snapshot, pin search_path and use a non-BYPASSRLS runtime role. The modules record the search_path but cannot enforce caller order by themselves.
The Workflow Quality-return source returns scoped receipt rows; the consumer must still run the full TypeScript-equivalent join, current IAM/purchase checks and post-effect revalidation.
The Files policy is an inner target-scope decision only; current assignment, attachment registry, target authority and Quality purchase capability remain caller-owned and unmounted.
The Runtime roster validator is not a sealed attestation or database identity grant.
No authenticated browser, gateway, production or staging journey was run.
Global cargo clippy remains red on unrelated worktree test/source warnings (for example rust-record-source unused mut and postgres_record_origin type complexity); this bundle does not touch them.
